routes.description: Establish that determinism and indeterminism both fail to provide the conscious authorship and same-circumstances alternatives integral to free will, and that practical capacities or accountability conventions do not supply what is missing.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if unauthored causes, constitutive luck, and unconscious processes defeat ultimate authorship while randomness supplies no control, leaving compatibilist competence and social regulation unable to establish free will in the disputed sense.

motionBridge.description: Show that neither causal determination nor indeterminacy permits the authorship and alternative possibilities required for free will and ultimate moral responsibility.

centralBridges.description: Establish that preserving useful capacities under the name free will omits the first-person authorship and actual ability to have done otherwise that motivate the dispute.
Show that genes, environment, prior brain states, and unconscious processes produce character and choice without being authored by the agent.
Distinguish useful accountability and behavioral regulation from genuine authorship or ultimate moral responsibility for causally produced conduct.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Show that tracing conduct to earlier choices only moves the authorship problem backward, while microscopic contingencies expose pervasive causal luck.
Show that randomness adds no ownership and that sufficiently informative advance prediction would expose rather than create conscious authorship.

routes.description: Establish that freedom worth preserving is the graded, naturalistic competence to deliberate, respond to reasons, exercise self-control, and undertake obligations, none of which requires exemption from deterministic causation.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if reasons-responsive control supports meaningful agency and calibrated responsibility, while demands for absolute self-creation, exact-replay alternatives, or indeterministic choice are shown unnecessary to the distinctions and practices free will must preserve.

motionBridge.description: Show that reasons-responsive agency supplies a determinism-compatible form of freedom sufficient for meaningful control and moral responsibility.

centralBridges.description: Define free agency through functioning capacities for reflection, ordered desire, attention, self-control, learning, and responsiveness to reasons.
Show that genuine control and temporally extended authorship do not require control of every background condition or awareness of every implementing microprocess.
Ground responsibility in graded competence, obligations, justified reliance, and stable consequentialist practices rather than absolute metaphysical desert.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Explain ability to do otherwise through robust competencies and relevantly similar circumstances rather than atom-for-atom replay of the universe.
Show that quantum indeterminacy adds no morally relevant freedom unavailable from deterministic deliberation, control, and practical randomness.

sections.title: The Concept and Stakes of Free Will
sections.rationale: This issue determines whether naturalistic conceptual revision preserves the phenomenon at stake or changes the subject by omitting authorship and same-circumstances alternatives.

sections.title: Reasons-Responsive Competence and Bounded Control
sections.rationale: This issue tests whether deliberation, self-control, obligations, and responsiveness to reasons constitute genuine agency despite dependence on uncontrolled causal conditions.

sections.title: Authorship, Constitutive Luck, and Neural Causation
sections.rationale: This issue addresses whether genes, environment, prior brain states, anomalous lapses, and unconscious implementation defeat authorship or remain compatible with temporally extended self-governance.

sections.title: Alternative Possibilities, Replay, and Randomness
sections.rationale: This issue compares exact-replay ability with competence across relevantly similar circumstances and tests whether deterministic chaos or indeterminacy contributes anything morally significant.

sections.title: Moral Responsibility, Accountability, and Social Practice
sections.rationale: This issue determines whether causal explanation universally exculpates or whether graded competence, reliance, deterrence, rehabilitation, and stable institutions sustain responsibility without absolute authorship.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-007.proposition: Compatibilism omits the first-person authorship and same-circumstances ability to do otherwise that motivate the free-will problem, preserving useful capacities under the name of a different phenomenon.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-009.proposition: When a minute synaptic condition can redirect a consequential choice and an entire life, the agent's dependence on unauthored physical causes undermines the ordinary picture of autonomous authorship.

chunk-002:c002-01.proposition: Microscopic neural variation can determine life-changing actions even when a decision is not already balanced on a knife-edge, so causal chance cannot be confined to inconsequential toss-ups.

chunk-002:c002-02.proposition: Libertarian free will maps onto neither determinism nor indeterminism, while graded lawful capacities constitute a compatibilist redefinition rather than the freedom denied by that dilemma.

chunk-002:c002-03.proposition: Complete neurophysiological explanation would make ordinary wrongdoing exculpatory in the same relevant sense as behavior caused by a brain tumor because the decisive neural condition was not authored by the agent.

chunk-002:c002-05.proposition: Differences in voluntary control and reasons-responsive capacity are real, but agents do not author the genes, environment, conversations, or prior brain states that determine those capacities and their responses.

chunk-002:c002-07.proposition: A highly competent agent's rare failure may attract maximal blame while being least representative of that agent, exposing luck rather than stable competence as the explanation of the anomalous act.

chunk-002:c002-09.proposition: Relocating responsibility for an anomalous lapse to an earlier avoidable choice does not restore authorship, because closer examination makes each prior choice another causally produced, unauthored event.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-04.proposition: Punishment and stable expectations can influence behavior, yet fuller causal understanding would reveal wrongdoing and reactions to it as unchosen brain states rather than genuine self-authorship.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-10.proposition: Neither deterministic chaos nor practical randomization supplies upstream ownership, and sufficiently early neural prediction would expose conscious action as the result rather than the author of its causal process.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-001.proposition: The freedom relevant to moral responsibility is compatible with determinism, whereas libertarian or indeterminist freedom is an unnecessary philosophical fantasy.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-003.proposition: Compatibilism can preserve a naturalistic concept of free will by discarding inherited magical commitments without discarding the real phenomenon those commitments misdescribe.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-006.proposition: Responsible agency consists in graded capacities including ordered desires, flexible attention, responsiveness to reasons, and self-control, which distinguish free from impaired agents regardless of determinism.

chunk-002:c002-06.proposition: Genuine control does not require control over every background condition; it consists in competently responding to given conditions and sustaining cultivated self-governance.

chunk-002:c002-10.proposition: People can author themselves within limits by working with unchosen materials and can accept moral responsibility even though luck contributes to their development and failures.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-02.proposition: Responsibility need not be absolute because free will and legal accountability are pragmatic, consequentialist institutions calibrated to actual human capacities.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-03.proposition: Even curable or causally diagnosed wrongdoing may warrant predictable penalties because deterrence, public confidence, and cooperative institutions depend on stable and enforceable rules.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-06.proposition: Conscious authorship operates through temporally extended, high-level control and therefore does not require awareness or control of every neural microprocess implementing an action.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-08.proposition: An agent could have done otherwise by possessing competence across a real range of actions, without requiring an atom-for-atom replay of the identical physical universe.

chunk-004:chunk-004-candidate-001.proposition: The difference between deterministic chaos and quantum indeterminacy makes no moral difference, so indeterminacy supplies no freedom unavailable from deterministic processes.
